h: Hidden Torah Light and the Wine of Shabbos

p: Now at this second Shabbos meal
בָּא לְכָל אֶחָד הַשִּׂמְחָה וְהָאוֹר בַּלֵּב
joy and light come into the heart of each person,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב אוֹר צַדִּיקִים יִשְׂמָח (מִשְׁלֵי יג, ט)
as is written, "The light of the righteous rejoices" (Mishlei 13:9).
Although it is stated (end of the first chapter of Taanis, 15a):
"the righteous to light and the upright to joy,"
so that the righteous merit only light,
nevertheless, when the tzaddik merits light,
הַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת אוֹר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
that is, the aspect of the light of Torah she'b'al peh,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב אוֹר זָרוּעַ לַצַּדִּיק (תְּהִלִּים צז, יא)
as written, "Light is sown for the tzaddik" (Tehillim 97:11),
שֶׁגְּנָזוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לָאוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן
for HaKadosh Baruch Hu hid away the primordial light
and it is revealed to the tzaddik;
"For in much wisdom is much anger";
and through this the heart is made upright
as it says, "And for the upright of heart, joy."
And at the meal of Shabbos night we say,
for then too we merit the primordial light,
רַק שָׁם הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַדְלָקַת הַנֵּרוֹת
Only there it is through the lighting of the candles,
that is, effort on the part of man.
This is not so with the second meal,
which is the aspect of Atika:
then "may His light rest upon it,"
"to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you";
and from this comes joy, as stated.
for with regard to Hashem Yisbarach,
it is small relative to what is greater than it.
the aspect of the holiness of Atika.
הַיְינוּ בְּחִינַת קְדוּשַּׁת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
that is, the aspect of the holiness of Torah she'b'al peh,
which is "the wine I have mixed";
and it is the dew of Atika,
"My word shall distill like the dew" (Devarim 32:2):
שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר אֵיךְ שֶׁיּוֹרֵד מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
which is not perceived as it comes down from heaven,
רַק מִמַּה שֶּׁרוֹאִים לַחוּתוֹ עַל הָאָרֶץ
but only from seeing its moisture on the ground.
although it comes from their own mouths,
into the hearts of the Sages.
And in the Midrash Rabbah (this parsha, Bamidbar Rabbah 2:3):
הֱבִיאַנִי אֶל בֵּית הַיָּיִן (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב, ד)
'He brought me to the house of wine' (Shir HaShirim 2:4)?
Like a king who had a storehouse
and found it all vinegar, etc.;
so too, of the seventy nations,
He found the wine in Yisrael, etc.
And the numerical value of 'yayin' is seventy;
and of all of them, 'and his banner over me is love,'" etc.
And further on the Midrash Rabbah says:
"'The house of wine' — this is Sinai,
as it says, 'and drink of the wine I have mixed.'"
And so it is expounded in the holy Zohar
So how does it say that "yayin" equals seventy,
like the number of the seventy nations?
But in truth, in all the nations
there is found a spark of words of Torah
וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כּוּלָּם (נְחֶמְיָה ט, ו)
"And You give life to them all" (Nechemiah 9:6);
וְעִיקַּר הַחַיִּים הוּא עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
and the essence of life is through words of Torah.
And when Adam HaRishon was created,
and had the downfall not occurred,
all the nations would have been
and would have been the aspect of wine.
and of all of them, "and his banner over me is love,"
and this is "the wine of the Oral Torah."
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדָּרַשׁ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אַחַר כָּךְ
And as the Midrash Rabbah expounds afterward:
"the Torah, which is expounded in forty-nine ways,
וּמ״ט פָּנִים הוּא רַק בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And forty-nine ways exist only in Torah she'b'al peh;
which is not so with Torah she'bichsav,
which is written down and set,
and does not have many faces.
And this is "the house of wine"
over the whole world, the seventy nations;
שֶׁרַק בָּהֶם נִשְׁאַר הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
for only in them did Torah she'b'al peh remain,
"'The nobles of the people dug it
with the lawgiver, with their staffs' (Bamidbar 21:18):
for the Nesi'im would stand over it
each one to his tribe," etc.
And this is from the well,
which alludes to Torah she'b'al peh,
the number forty-nine ways, as stated.
And this is "and with the good wine,"
which is also the primordial light
that the heart is made upright
וְאָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה ב, ו)
And afterward the Midrash says (Bamidbar Rabbah 2:6):
'He found him in a desert land' (Devarim 32:10):
מָצָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
did HaKadosh Baruch Hu find in Yisrael,
as it says, 'Like grapes in the wilderness
the world was a desert, etc.;
the world was desolation and night," etc.
That is, Yisrael are called grapes,
for in them is found Torah she'b'al peh,
like the wine in the grapes.
He encircled him with the Clouds of Glory;
He instructed him — He made them understand words of Torah."
which is the aspect of surrounding light,
corresponds to the meal of Erev Shabbos night,
when we say, "that shines upon our heads"
"He instructed him — He made them understand words of Torah"
corresponds to the meal of Shabbos morning,
then we say, "May His light rest upon it,"
for the words of Torah enter the depths of the heart.
How far did He guard them?
How far did He protect them?
As it were, as the pupil of His eye, etc.;
and He descends and dwells among them."
And it explains "the pupil of His eye"
as the Mishkan and the Ohel Moed.
And this is in the manner of what is said,
וְהָיוּ עֵינַי וְלִבִּי שָׁם כָּל הַיָּמִים
"And My eyes and My heart shall be there all the days"
and it corresponds to the middah of Malchus:
אֲנִי ה׳ הַשּׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
"I, Hashem, Who dwells among the Bnei Yisrael,"
which is the holiness of Shabbos;
and this middah is called "the pupil of the eye"
